rows.practice: carries out field and laboratory investigations safely and ethically, identifies rocks, minerals and fossils, records observations and processes data with fitting numerical and qualitative methods
rows.knowledge: the core paradigms of geological time, plate tectonics and evolution and how matter and energy move between rock, water, air, ice and life
rows.identity: an environmental scientist in training who works to fieldwork codes of conduct, completes risk assessments with confidence and acts ethically, sustainably and within the law

rows.practice: plans and runs an independent project on an environmental question, framing hypotheses to design investigations and modelling incomplete field or subsurface data across space and time
rows.knowledge: how uncertainty in data and in system responses bears on decisions about resources, hazards and climate change, weighed across disciplines and within social, economic and environmental settings
rows.identity: an environmental practitioner who questions the ethics and colonial legacy of the discipline and makes a persuasive, evidence-led case that can sway environmental decisions

rows.practice: develops and leads an independent research project on a significant practical environmental question, probing the literature alone and applying techniques and data to varied problems
rows.knowledge: a substantial specialism in one aspect of earth or environmental science, built on first-degree competencies and on the research literature of that area
rows.identity: a specialist earth or environmental scientist who leads own research and grows into a more employable professional in a chosen field (ing's reading)

digest.definition: Earth sciences, environmental sciences and environmental studies are treated together as ES3, with enough overlap for one statement
distinctiveFeatures: Earth sciences, environmental sciences and environmental studies are treated together as ES3, with enough overlap for one statement
The setting is the climate emergency, biodiversity loss and wider threats to nature; graduates act on sound science with fairness in view
Environment is read broadly, covering human and non-human life
The subjects study physical, chemical and biological Earth systems to learn from the past and shape the future, across scales of space and time, through systems thinking
They are practical and field-based, with observation and analysis to support decisions under uncertainty
They are multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary, overlapping with biology, chemistry, geography, informatics and physics
Sustainability is at their root and at their core
EDI is subject matter as well as practice, with attention to colonial legacies and other ways of knowing

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: EDI as subject knowledge and practice: removing barriers to field and lab participation, decolonising the curriculum, valuing other ways of knowing, and a route to justice through the SDGs (D1, 1.2, 1.8, 1.9, 2.1)

subjectSpecific.text: You can expect to learn what sustainable development and systems thinking mean and how they are used in Earth science.
You can expect to learn how the Earth and the other planets formed and how they fit into the solar system.
You can expect to understand the big ideas of Earth science: that present processes explain the past, how vast geological time is, how life evolved and how plates move.
You can expect to learn how geological time is measured and divided, what the fossil record shows and which major events shaped Earth's history.
You can expect to learn what the solid Earth, oceans, atmosphere, ice and living world are made of and how matter and energy move between them.
You can expect to understand the biological, chemical and physical processes that explain how the Earth and other planets work.
You can expect to study structures, materials and processes and how they change across time and place, from small to large scales.
You can expect to learn how igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rocks form.
You can expect to learn to identify rocks, minerals, fossils and geological structures and to name and classify them correctly.
You can expect to learn to collect and analyse data from above and below ground and to model and extend them across space and time, even when they are incomplete.
You can expect to learn to observe in the field, in person or virtually, and to interpret what you see by reasoning from first principles.
You can expect to learn to survey and take measurements in the field and the laboratory with numerical methods and instruments.
You can expect to learn to work with both qualitative and numerical data and to judge how good and how certain your data are.
You can expect to understand how Earth science helps manage natural resources and lessen and adapt to hazards such as climate change.
You can expect to become aware that what you learn and how it is used sit within wider social, economic and environmental concerns.
You can expect to explore the ethical questions raised by Earth science's past and present uses, join current debates and understand why decolonising the subject matters.
You can expect to understand why equality, diversity and inclusion matter in how Earth science is done.
You can expect to learn the codes of practice for fieldwork and to complete health and safety risk assessments with confidence.
You can expect to learn what sustainable development and systems thinking mean and how they are used in environmental work.
You can expect to study the Earth's systems and processes as a connected whole.
You can expect to learn the principles of sustainability and how to manage the use of resources sustainably.
You can expect to understand how looking over different timescales, from geological to future, changes how you judge effects on ecosystems.
You can expect to understand how human effects on the environment, and responses to change, play out from global to local scales.
You can expect to learn how living things in natural and managed ecosystems depend on each other.
You can expect to learn how development helps and harms the environment and which tools can manage those effects.
You can expect to learn how environmental change affects people, other species and the things we build.
You can expect to learn to monitor, model and manage environmental change, whether natural or caused by people.
You can expect to learn how to forecast, reduce and manage risks from a changing environment and from human pressure.
You can expect to understand uncertainty and how it affects decisions now and later.
You can expect to learn how institutions, organisations, governments and other stakeholders manage and regulate human effects on the environment.
You can expect to understand how your subject helps manage resources and lessen and adapt to hazards such as climate change.
You can expect to learn to observe in the field, in person or virtually, and to interpret what you see by reasoning from first principles.
You can expect to learn to work with both qualitative and numerical data and to judge how good and how certain your data are.
You can expect to become aware that what you learn and how it is used sit within wider social, economic and environmental concerns.
You can expect to explore the ethical questions raised by your subject's past and present uses, join current debates and understand why decolonising it matters.
You can expect to understand why equality, diversity and inclusion matter in how your subject is practised.
You can expect to learn the codes of practice for fieldwork and to complete health and safety risk assessments with confidence.
You can expect to study scientifically the physical, chemical, biological and human processes that act on ecosystems.
You can expect to learn the main environmental processes from the global scale down to single organisms and, where useful, molecules and atoms.
You can expect to learn a scientific approach, drawing on several disciplines, to recognising, understanding and managing the structure, processes and ecosystems of the Earth.
You can expect to learn to use scientific information and technical tools to support decisions and environmental management.
You can expect to learn to observe in the field, in person or virtually, and to interpret what you see from first principles.
You can expect to learn to survey and take measurements in the field and the laboratory with numerical methods and instruments.
You can expect to learn the history of environmental change, both natural and caused by people, and the evidence for it today.
You can expect to understand the social, political and economic consequences of how people treat the environment.
You can expect to understand how the environment and human cultures and values shape each other.

headingPath: Context and characteristics of an Earth Sciences, Environmental Sciences and Environmental Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: graduates in ES3 subjects
statements.about: decisions grounded in sound science and fairness
statements.paraphrase: Set against the climate emergency, biodiversity loss and other pressures on nature, which call for action from global policy to local practice, ES3 graduates will be required to make sure that actions and decisions rest on good science and weigh equity, equality, diversity and inclusion, so that solutions last and are sustainable.

forPractitioner.text: Prepare students for a working world in which they will be required to ground decisions in sound science and to weigh equity and inclusion, so that the solutions they propose last; the climate and biodiversity crises are the setting for the whole course.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be expected, in your working life, to make sure that the decisions you take part in rest on sound science and treat people fairly, so that the solutions you help to build last.

headingPath: Context and characteristics of an Earth Sciences, Environmental Sciences and Environmental Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: readers and users of the statement
statements.about: reading environment broadly
statements.paraphrase: The word environment, wherever the statement uses it, should be read broadly, so that it covers every living thing, human and non-human.

forPractitioner.text: Read environment, in every part of the statement, as covering all living things, people and other species alike, and carry that breadth into course documents.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a note to readers on how to read a term in the document, not a standard for the student

headingPath: Context and characteristics of an Earth Sciences, Environmental Sciences and Environmental Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: ES3 academic communities
statements.about: removing barriers to taking part in the disciplines
statements.paraphrase: EDI belongs to the ES3 subjects both as how they are taught and as knowledge in its own right; diverse groups matter to learning communities but face many barriers, which ES3 communities have a duty to challenge and help take down, perhaps using equality impact assessments, and they can commit to safe, inclusive settings that welcome diversity and co-produced curricula.

forPractitioner.text: Treat equality, diversity and inclusion as subject content and as practice; your teaching community carries a duty to challenge and help remove barriers to taking part, for example through equality impact assessments, and to build safe, inclusive spaces where curricula can be co-produced with students.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the academic community and the course, not a standard for the student

headingPath: Context and characteristics of an Earth Sciences, Environmental Sciences and Environmental Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: graduates of ES3 programmes
statements.about: cultural awareness, ethics and openness to other ways of knowing
statements.paraphrase: EDI can be explored by challenging the disciplines' identities and stereotypes, colonial legacies included, diversifying curricula and valuing other cultures' knowledge and lived experience; the subjects serve justice through the SDGs, so programmes develop graduates who are culturally aware, ethical and respectful and can reflect on equality; they will also think in systems, adapt, work across disciplines and stay open to other ways of thinking.

forPractitioner.text: Use the discipline itself to explore EDI, by questioning its stereotypes and colonial history and valuing other knowledge systems; graduates will be culturally aware, ethical and respectful and able to reflect on equality in the subject; they will also think in systems, adapt and work across disciplines.

forBeneficiary.text: You will become culturally aware, act ethically and with respect, reflect on equality in your subject, think in terms of whole systems, adapt to change and stay open to ways of knowing that differ from your own.

statements.about: using the joint ESD guidance

forPractitioner.text: When you build sustainable development into an ES3 curriculum, you should use the joint QAA and Advance HE ESD guidance for teaching, key competencies, outcomes and assessment.

statements.about: using the enterprise and entrepreneurship guidance

forPractitioner.text: When you build employability, enterprise and entrepreneurship into an ES3 course, you should use QAA's enterprise and entrepreneurship education guidance.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a pointer for course designers, not a standard for the student

headingPath: Distinctive features of an Earth Sciences, Environmental Sciences and Environmental Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: course and field programme design
statements.about: accessible design, adjustments and inclusive risk assessment
statements.paraphrase: Accessibility means designing curriculum and teaching so nobody is shut out; barriers, often overlapping, are tackled deliberately so all learners can take part and do well; inclusive design should let everyone take part, though flexibility and reasonable adjustments may still be needed; field and laboratory work can exclude, so courses may need several strategies and accessible technology; risk assessments should cover health, safety and well-being, including risks to students with protected characteristics; blended options help a wide range of learners.

forPractitioner.text: Design curricula and field programmes so that no one is excluded: inclusive design should let all learners take part, with flexibility and reasonable adjustments where needed; plan for the barriers labs and fieldwork can raise and use accessible technology; make risk assessments cover health, safety and well-being, including risks a student with protected characteristics may face.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of an Earth Sciences, Environmental Sciences and Environmental Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: honours and integrated master's students
statements.about: progression to the threshold and the integrated master's year
statements.paraphrase: Across an honours degree (at FHEQ level 6, or SCQF level 10 in Scotland) each student moves up year by year under each institution's rules, reaching set levels of knowledge, expertise and experience each year that build towards meeting every threshold subject-specific and generic skill; an integrated master's (FHEQ level 7; SCQF level 11) adds a year, after which students are able to show stronger critical thinking, evaluation and independence; early exit awards are possible, and Scottish honours degrees usually last four years.

forPractitioner.text: Plan each year so attainment builds towards every threshold skill by the end of the honours degree (FHEQ level 6; SCQF level 10); in an integrated master's (FHEQ level 7; SCQF level 11), the extra year will leave students able to show stronger critical thinking, evaluation and independence.

forBeneficiary.text: Each year of your honours degree will build your knowledge and experience towards the full set of skills expected at graduation; if you take an integrated master's, your extra year will leave you thinking more critically, evaluating more sharply and working more independently.

headingPath: Distinctive features of an Earth Sciences, Environmental Sciences and Environmental Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: undergraduates with a second-class degree or above
statements.about: readiness for postgraduate and cross-disciplinary study
statements.paraphrase: Where it applies, a graduate with at least a second-class degree would normally be expected to be able and ready to go on to postgraduate study in ES3 or related sustainability fields, and to enter courses that combine disciplines.

forPractitioner.text: A graduate with a second-class honours degree or better would normally be expected to be capable of and ready for postgraduate study in ES3 or related sustainability fields, including cross-disciplinary courses.

forBeneficiary.text: If you graduate with a second-class degree or higher, you would normally be ready to go on to postgraduate study in your subject, in a related sustainability field or on a course that combines disciplines.

headingPath: Distinctive features of an Earth Sciences, Environmental Sciences and Environmental Studies degree

statements.appliesTo: joint honours undergraduates
statements.about: joint honours and the skill lists
statements.paraphrase: Students on joint honours will reach part of the subject-specific and generic skills for ES3 and add further skills from their other subject.

forPractitioner.text: Joint honours students will achieve some of the ES3 subject-specific and generic skills, with others drawn from the partner subject; map which ones each route covers.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study ES3 in a joint honours degree, you will gain some of its subject and general skills and add others from your second subject.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: sustainable development and systems thinking
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of the ideas and uses of sustainable development and systems thinking, taught in a way that should match the joint QAA and Advance HE guidance on ESD.

forPractitioner.text: Teach what sustainable development and systems thinking are and how they are put to use; this should line up with the joint ESD guidance from QAA and Advance HE.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn what sustainable development and systems thinking mean and how they are used in Earth science.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: how the Earth and planets formed
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of how the Earth and the other planets came into being and where they sit in the solar system.

forPractitioner.text: Cover the origin of the Earth and other planets and their position in the solar system.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn how the Earth and the other planets formed and how they fit into the solar system.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: the central paradigms of the Earth sciences
statements.paraphrase: Understanding of the field's core paradigms: uniformitarianism, the span of geological time, evolution and plate tectonics.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the field's core paradigms, from uniformitarianism and deep time to evolution and plate tectonics.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to understand the big ideas of Earth science: that present processes explain the past, how vast geological time is, how life evolved and how plates move.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: geological time and Earth history
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of geological time: stratigraphic principles and the column, the fossil record, dating methods, how fast processes run and the major events of Earth history.

forPractitioner.text: Cover stratigraphy and the stratigraphic column, the fossil record, geochronology, process rates and major events in Earth history.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn how geological time is measured and divided, what the fossil record shows and which major events shaped Earth's history.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: Earth spheres and the cycling of matter and energy
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of the make-up of the solid Earth, oceans and waters, air, ice and living world, the processes acting in each and how matter and energy cycle through them.

forPractitioner.text: Teach how the solid Earth, hydrosphere, atmosphere, cryosphere and biosphere are built and composed and the processes and cycles linking them.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn what the solid Earth, oceans, atmosphere, ice and living world are made of and how matter and energy move between them.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: processes behind Earth and planetary systems
statements.paraphrase: Understanding of the biological, chemical and physical processes on which knowledge of Earth and planetary systems rests.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the biological, chemical and physical processes that explain how Earth and planetary systems work.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to understand the biological, chemical and physical processes that explain how the Earth and other planets work.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: variation in time and space at fitting scales
statements.paraphrase: Understanding of structures, materials and processes with attention to how they vary over time and space at suitable scales.

forPractitioner.text: Teach structures, materials and processes so students appreciate how they vary in time and space at appropriate scales.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to study structures, materials and processes and how they change across time and place, from small to large scales.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: formation of the main rock types
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of how igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rocks form.

forPractitioner.text: Cover the formation of igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rocks.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn how igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rocks form.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: identifying rocks, minerals, fossils and structures
statements.paraphrase: Recognising rocks, minerals, fossils and geological structures and using the right terms, names and classifications for them.

forPractitioner.text: Teach students to identify rocks, minerals, fossils and geological structures and to use the field's terminology, nomenclature and classification.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn to identify rocks, minerals, fossils and geological structures and to name and classify them correctly.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: collecting and modelling Earth data in four dimensions
statements.paraphrase: Gathering and analysing data from the surface and subsurface, then presenting, handling, modelling and extrapolating these often incomplete data across space and time.

forPractitioner.text: Teach collection and analysis of surface and subsurface data and their presentation, manipulation, modelling and extrapolation in four dimensions, including incomplete data.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn to collect and analyse data from above and below ground and to model and extend them across space and time, even when they are incomplete.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: interpreting field data from first principles
statements.paraphrase: Observing and interpreting field data, gathered in person or virtually, by reasoning from first principles.

forPractitioner.text: Train students to observe and interpret field data, in situ or virtual, from first principles.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn to observe in the field, in person or virtually, and to interpret what you see by reasoning from first principles.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: surveying and measuring in the field and laboratory
statements.paraphrase: Surveying and measuring in the field and the laboratory with quantitative and instrumental methods.

forPractitioner.text: Teach surveying and measurement in field and laboratory using quantitative and instrumental techniques.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn to survey and take measurements in the field and the laboratory with numerical methods and instruments.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: data use, quality and uncertainty
statements.paraphrase: Working with qualitative and quantitative data and datasets, and knowing how to assess data quality and uncertainty.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the use of qualitative and quantitative data and datasets and how to assess data quality and uncertainty.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn to work with both qualitative and numerical data and to judge how good and how certain your data are.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: Earth sciences in resources, hazards and climate change
statements.paraphrase: Understanding why the Earth sciences matter for managing resources and for reducing and adapting to environmental hazards, climate change among them.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the role of the Earth sciences in resource management and in mitigating and adapting to environmental hazards, including climate change.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to understand how Earth science helps manage natural resources and lessen and adapt to hazards such as climate change.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: the wider socioeconomic and environmental context
statements.paraphrase: Awareness that the subject's knowledge and its uses are weighed within a broader social, economic and environmental setting.

forPractitioner.text: Develop students' awareness that the subject and its application sit within a wider socioeconomic and environmental context.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to become aware that what you learn and how it is used sit within wider social, economic and environmental concerns.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: ethics, legacy and decolonisation of the discipline
statements.paraphrase: Understanding the ethical questions raised by the discipline's history and uses, taking part in current debates and seeing why decolonisation is needed.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the ethics of the discipline's legacy and uses, engage students in current debates and help them see the case for decolonisation.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to explore the ethical questions raised by Earth science's past and present uses, join current debates and understand why decolonising the subject matters.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: EDI in the practice of the discipline
statements.paraphrase: Understanding why equality, diversity and inclusivity matter in how the discipline is practised.

forPractitioner.text: Teach why equality, diversity and inclusivity matter in Earth science practice.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to understand why equality, diversity and inclusion matter in how Earth science is done.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in Earth sciences
statements.about: fieldwork codes and risk assessment
statements.paraphrase: Awareness of codes of practice for fieldwork and the ability to complete health and safety risk assessments with confidence.

forPractitioner.text: Teach fieldwork codes of practice and have students complete health and safety risk assessments confidently.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn the codes of practice for fieldwork and to complete health and safety risk assessments with confidence.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: sustainable development and systems thinking
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of the ideas and uses of sustainable development and systems thinking, taught in a way that should match the joint QAA and Advance HE guidance on ESD.

forPractitioner.text: Teach what sustainable development and systems thinking are and how they are put to use; this should line up with the joint ESD guidance from QAA and Advance HE.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn what sustainable development and systems thinking mean and how they are used in environmental work.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: a holistic view of Earth systems
statements.paraphrase: Studying Earth's systems and processes as a whole, with their complexity and links.

forPractitioner.text: Take a holistic approach to the complexity and interconnections of Earth's systems and processes.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to study the Earth's systems and processes as a connected whole.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: sustainability principles and resource cycles
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of sustainability principles and of sustainable ways to manage natural and human-driven cycles of resource use.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the principles of sustainability and sustainable approaches to managing natural and human-induced resource cycles.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn the principles of sustainability and how to manage the use of resources sustainably.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: timescale and impacts on ecosystems
statements.paraphrase: Understanding how the timescale considered, from geological to future, shapes the effects of natural and human activity on ecosystems.

forPractitioner.text: Teach why timescale, geological, present, short and long term and future, matters to the impacts of natural and human activities on ecosystems.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to understand how looking over different timescales, from geological to future, changes how you judge effects on ecosystems.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: spatial scale of human impacts
statements.paraphrase: Understanding the spatial scale, global to local, of human effects on the environment and of responses to change.

forPractitioner.text: Teach how human effects on the environment, and responses to change, differ from the global scale down to the local.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to understand how human effects on the environment, and responses to change, play out from global to local scales.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: interdependence of organisms in ecosystems
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of how all organisms in natural and managed ecosystems connect with and depend on each other.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the interconnections and interdependencies of organisms in natural and managed ecosystems.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn how living things in natural and managed ecosystems depend on each other.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: impacts of development and tools to manage them
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of the good and harmful effects of development on the environment and of the management tools for dealing with them.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the positive and negative environmental impacts of development and the management tools that address them.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn how development helps and harms the environment and which tools can manage those effects.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: effects of environmental change on people, other species and infrastructure
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of how environmental change affects people, other species and infrastructure.

forPractitioner.text: Teach how environmental change affects people, other species and built infrastructure.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn how environmental change affects people, other species and the things we build.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: monitoring, modelling and managing environmental change
statements.paraphrase: Monitoring, modelling and managing environmental change and behaviour, natural and human-induced.

forPractitioner.text: Teach monitoring, modelling and management of natural and human-induced environmental change and behaviour.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn to monitor, model and manage environmental change, whether natural or caused by people.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: predicting and managing environmental risk
statements.paraphrase: Knowing how to forecast, reduce and manage the risks posed by a changing environment and human pressure.

forPractitioner.text: Teach how to predict, mitigate and manage risks from environmental change and human pressures.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn how to forecast, reduce and manage risks from a changing environment and from human pressure.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: uncertainty in decision-making
statements.paraphrase: Understanding uncertainty and how it bears on decisions now and in future.

forPractitioner.text: Teach what uncertainty is and how it affects present and future decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to understand uncertainty and how it affects decisions now and later.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: institutions and governance of human impacts
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of the part institutions, organisations, governance and other stakeholders play in managing and regulating human effects on the environment.

forPractitioner.text: Teach how institutions, organisations, governance structures and stakeholders manage and regulate what people do to the environment.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn how institutions, organisations, governments and other stakeholders manage and regulate human effects on the environment.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: the subjects in resources, hazards and climate change
statements.paraphrase: Understanding why environmental sciences and studies matter for managing resources and for reducing and adapting to environmental hazards, climate change among them.

forPractitioner.text: Teach why environmental science and environmental studies matter for managing resources and for reducing and adapting to hazards, climate change included.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to understand how your subject helps manage resources and lessen and adapt to hazards such as climate change.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: interpreting field data from first principles
statements.paraphrase: Observing and interpreting field data, gathered in person or virtually, by reasoning from first principles.

forPractitioner.text: Train students to observe and interpret field data, in situ or virtual, from first principles.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn to observe in the field, in person or virtually, and to interpret what you see by reasoning from first principles.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: data use, quality and uncertainty
statements.paraphrase: Working with qualitative and quantitative data and datasets, and knowing how to assess data quality and uncertainty.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the use of qualitative and quantitative data and datasets and how to assess data quality and uncertainty.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn to work with both qualitative and numerical data and to judge how good and how certain your data are.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: digital skills and technology
statements.paraphrase: Building digital skills and technology use that are relevant and fit for purpose.

forPractitioner.text: Develop relevant, appropriate digital skills and use of technology.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to build the digital skills and confidence with technology your field needs.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: the wider socioeconomic and environmental context
statements.paraphrase: Awareness that the subject's knowledge and its uses are weighed within a broader social, economic and environmental setting.

forPractitioner.text: Develop students' awareness that the subject and its application sit within a wider socioeconomic and environmental context.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to become aware that what you learn and how it is used sit within wider social, economic and environmental concerns.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: ethics, legacy and decolonisation of the discipline
statements.paraphrase: Understanding the ethical questions raised by the discipline's history and uses, taking part in current debates and seeing why decolonisation is needed.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the ethics of the discipline's legacy and uses, engage students in current debates and help them see the case for decolonisation.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to explore the ethical questions raised by your subject's past and present uses, join current debates and understand why decolonising it matters.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: EDI in the practice of the discipline
statements.paraphrase: Understanding why equality, diversity and inclusivity matter in how the discipline is practised.

forPractitioner.text: Teach why equality, diversity and inclusivity matter in environmental practice.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to understand why equality, diversity and inclusion matter in how your subject is practised.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences or environmental studies
statements.about: fieldwork codes and risk assessment
statements.paraphrase: Awareness of codes of practice for fieldwork and the ability to complete health and safety risk assessments with confidence.

forPractitioner.text: Teach fieldwork codes of practice and have students complete health and safety risk assessments confidently.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn the codes of practice for fieldwork and to complete health and safety risk assessments with confidence.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences
statements.about: scientific study of processes acting on ecosystems
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge, from scientific study, of the physical, chemical, biological and human-driven processes that act on ecosystems.

forPractitioner.text: Include scientific study of the physical, chemical, biological and human-made processes that act on ecosystems.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to study scientifically the physical, chemical, biological and human processes that act on ecosystems.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences
statements.about: environmental processes from global to atomic scale
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of the main environmental processes at scales from the planet to the organism and, where it fits, down to molecules and atoms.

forPractitioner.text: Include major environmental processes across scales from global to organismal and, where relevant, to molecular and atomic levels.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn the main environmental processes from the global scale down to single organisms and, where useful, molecules and atoms.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences
statements.about: a scientific approach to Earth's structure, processes and ecosystems
statements.paraphrase: A scientific, multidisciplinary way to recognise, understand and manage the structure, processes and ecosystems of the Earth.

forPractitioner.text: Include a scientific, multidisciplinary approach to identifying, understanding and managing Earth's structure, processes and ecosystems.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn a scientific approach, drawing on several disciplines, to recognising, understanding and managing the structure, processes and ecosystems of the Earth.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences
statements.about: scientific information and tools for decisions
statements.paraphrase: Using scientific and technical information and tools to support decisions and environmental management.

forPractitioner.text: Include using scientific and technical information and tools to support decisions and environmental management.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn to use scientific information and technical tools to support decisions and environmental management.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences
statements.about: interpreting field data from first principles
statements.paraphrase: Observing and interpreting field data, gathered in person or virtually, by reasoning from first principles.

forPractitioner.text: Include observation and interpretation of field data, in situ or virtual, from first principles.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn to observe in the field, in person or virtually, and to interpret what you see from first principles.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental sciences
statements.about: surveying and measuring in the field and laboratory
statements.paraphrase: Surveying and measuring in the field and the laboratory with quantitative and instrumental methods.

forPractitioner.text: Include surveying and measurement in field and laboratory using quantitative and instrumental techniques.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn to survey and take measurements in the field and the laboratory with numerical methods and instruments.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental studies
statements.about: history and evidence of environmental change
statements.paraphrase: Knowledge of the history of environmental change, natural and human-driven, and the evidence for it now.

forPractitioner.text: Include the history and present evidence of natural and human-induced environmental change.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to learn the history of environmental change, both natural and caused by people, and the evidence for it today.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental studies
statements.about: social, political and economic implications
statements.paraphrase: Understanding the social, political and economic consequences of how people interact with the environment.

forPractitioner.text: Include the social, political and economic consequences of how people interact with the environment.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to understand the social, political and economic consequences of how people treat the environment.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in environmental studies
statements.about: environment, culture and values
statements.paraphrase: Understanding how the environment relates to human cultures and values.

forPractitioner.text: Include how the environment relates to human cultures and their values.

forBeneficiary.text: You can expect to understand how the environment and human cultures and values shape each other.

statements.appliesTo: ES3 courses
statements.about: outcomes reachable by the methods used and made clear
statements.paraphrase: The statement does not choose teaching or learning methods, but the outcomes should be reachable through the methods a course uses and set out clearly for learners.

forPractitioner.text: Choose your own teaching and learning methods, but check that students can reach the outcomes through them and that the outcomes are stated clearly to students.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: ES3 courses
statements.about: inclusive, fitting teaching methods
statements.paraphrase: Teaching and learning link within curriculum design, and the methods chosen should be inclusive and fit to build the knowledge and skills in sections 1 and 2; courses led by research or enquiry may build subject-based knowledge and skills.

forPractitioner.text: Pick teaching and learning methods that are inclusive and fit to develop the knowledge and skills sections 1 and 2 describe; research-led and enquiry-based designs are one option.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: ES3 courses and their field and practical activities
statements.about: fieldwork for all, inclusively designed with adjustments
statements.paraphrase: Practical work, above all fieldwork, is woven through the subjects, so courses give every student substantial field-based learning that builds skills such as visualising data in three dimensions and applying practical methods; field skills matter for ES3 careers and build transferable attributes; activities should be inclusive, and reasonable adjustments should be arranged where needed so all can take part.

forPractitioner.text: Give every student substantial fieldwork, integrated with theory; design field and practical activities to be inclusive, and arrange reasonable adjustments where required so that all students can take part in practical work and fieldwork.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: ES3 courses
statements.about: teaching grounded in ESD
statements.paraphrase: Sustainability is central to ES3, so teaching and learning should rest plainly on education for sustainable development and its methods should live out sustainable principles and solutions.

forPractitioner.text: Ground teaching and learning in education for sustainable development, and choose methods that themselves practise sustainable principles and solutions.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: higher education providers awarding ES3 honours degrees
statements.about: Annex D for performance above the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Most students will do much better than the threshold; each provider decides what evidence shows this and should use Annex D, QAA's descriptions of the four honours classifications (1st, 2:1, 2:2, 3rd) at FHEQ level 6 and FQHEIS level 10.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to go well beyond the threshold; set your own evidence for this and use Annex D's descriptions of first, upper second, lower second and third-class honours (FHEQ level 6; FQHEIS level 10).

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in judging classifications

headingPath: Threshold level: Intellectual skills (knowledge and understanding)

statements.about: subject theories, paradigms, concepts and principles
statements.paraphrase: Know and understand the theories, paradigms, concepts and principles particular to the subject.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates know and understand the subject's own theories, paradigms, concepts and principles.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate with honours, you will know and understand the main theories, paradigms, concepts and principles of your subject.

headingPath: Threshold level: Intellectual skills (knowledge and understanding)

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: testing findings against several sources of evidence
statements.paraphrase: Bring together evidence from varied sources to check findings and hypotheses.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates combine evidence from several sources to test findings and hypotheses.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to combine evidence from different sources to test findings and hypotheses.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: looking at issues across disciplines
statements.paraphrase: Weigh up and judge issues from several multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary angles.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates weigh up and judge issues from several multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary viewpoints.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to look at an issue from the viewpoints of several disciplines and judge them.

statements.about: analysing and critically evaluating information
statements.paraphrase: Analyse, combine, summarise, judge and critically evaluate information.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates analyse, synthesise, summarise, appraise and critically evaluate information.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to analyse, pull together, summarise and critically judge information.

headingPath: Threshold level: Intellectual skills (knowledge and understanding)

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: defining complex problems and weighing solutions
statements.paraphrase: Set out complex problems clearly, then work up and judge possible solutions.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates set out complex problems and work up and judge possible solutions.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to define a complex problem and come up with and judge possible solutions.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: hypotheses that shape investigations
statements.paraphrase: Form and test hypotheses that guide the design of investigations and experiments.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates form and test hypotheses and use them to shape and design investigations, experiments included.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to form and test hypotheses and use them to design investigations and experiments.

statements.about: an independent project with guidance
statements.paraphrase: Plan, carry out and present an independent project, with suitable guidance.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates plan, carry out and present an independent project, with suitable guidance.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will have planned, carried out and presented a project of your own, with suitable support.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will read academic work, data and other sources critically.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: handling uncertainty in data and systems
statements.paraphrase: Deal with uncertainty in data and in how systems respond, with confidence and competence.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates deal confidently and competently with uncertainty in data and in system responses.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to work confidently with uncertainty in data and in how systems behave.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: competent field and laboratory investigation
statements.paraphrase: Carry out field and laboratory investigations competently, as fits the course.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates conduct fieldwork and laboratory investigations competently, as appropriate to the course.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to carry out fieldwork and laboratory investigations competently.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: recording observations in field and laboratory
statements.paraphrase: Describe and record observations well in the field and the laboratory.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates describe and record observations effectively in field and laboratory.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to describe and record what you observe clearly in the field and the lab.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: logical interpretation of practical results
statements.paraphrase: Interpret and judge practical results logically.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates interpret and evaluate practical results logically.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to interpret and judge practical results logically.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: ethical and safe practical work
statements.paraphrase: Do laboratory and fieldwork ethically and safely, aware of the relevant codes of conduct and legal requirements.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates carry out lab and field work ethically and safely, aware of the codes of conduct and the law that apply.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will carry out lab and field work ethically and safely, knowing the codes of conduct and the law that apply.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: gathering and processing data
statements.paraphrase: Collect, prepare, process and interpret data with suitable methods.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates collect, prepare, process and interpret data with suitable techniques.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to collect, prepare, process and interpret data with the right methods.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: numerical, statistical and qualitative techniques
statements.paraphrase: Apply suitable numerical, statistical and qualitative methods.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates use appropriate numerical, statistical and qualitative techniques.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to use suitable numerical, statistical and qualitative methods.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: technologies for solving problems
statements.paraphrase: Use fitting technologies to tackle problems well.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates use appropriate technologies to address problems effectively.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to use the right technologies to tackle problems well.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: communicating with varied audiences and media
statements.paraphrase: Communicate well with different audiences in a range of formats and media.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates communicate effectively with varied audiences across formats and media.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, you will be able to communicate well with different audiences in different formats and media.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates in ES3 at the threshold
statements.about: interpersonal skills for teamwork
statements.paraphrase: Have sound interpersonal communication skills that make teamwork effective.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of integrated master's courses
statements.about: specialism and an independent research project
statements.paraphrase: Beyond the skills built over the course, integrated master's graduates will have gained a substantial specialism by developing and leading an independent research project, and will show they can probe the literature on their own, apply ideas, techniques and data to varied questions and design and run a project on a significant practical question.

forPractitioner.text: Integrated master's graduates will have built a significant specialism through an independent research project they develop and lead, and will show they can interrogate the literature alone and design and carry out a project on an important practical question.

forBeneficiary.text: In an integrated master's, you will build a real specialism by planning and leading your own research project, and you will show that you can search the literature independently, apply ideas, methods and data to different questions and design and run a project that tackles a practical problem.

statements.appliesTo: taught postgraduate (MSc or MA) students
statements.about: postgraduate depth in one aspect of the subject
statements.paraphrase: At taught postgraduate level (MSc or MA), students are expected to build on the competencies from their first degree and go deeper into one aspect of the subject, gaining knowledge and skills that make them more employable.

forPractitioner.text: Taught MSc or MA students will build on the undergraduate competencies above and focus in more depth on one aspect of the subject, gaining knowledge and skills that improve their employability.

forBeneficiary.text: On a taught master's, you will build on what you learned as an undergraduate and go deeper into one area of the subject, gaining knowledge and skills that strengthen your career prospects.
